newsitem.title: USA: Schlumberger sees charge, gain, to merge units.
newsitem.headline: Schlumberger sees charge, gain, to merge units.

text.p: Schlumberger Ltd., which is combining two related energy businesses, said Wednesday it will trim jobs, manufacturing facilities and products and post a credit and charges in the third quarter.
Schlumberger will take a $360 million credit as it recognises a portion of the U.S. income tax benefit related to its U.S. subsidiary's tax-loss carryforwards.
The company will take an after-tax charge of $300 million related primarily to its Electricity and Gas Management, and Geco-Prakla divisions.
Schlumberger will also record an after-tax charge of $58 million, including a loss on the divestiture of its remaining defence-related activity, certain asset impairments and other charges.

Within the Measurement & Systems business segment, the company said, the Electricity and Gas Management product lines have been combined into a single business to serve the rapidly changing energy supply sector more efficiently.
"Over the near term these items will have no material impact on the results of Schlumberger," said Chief Financial Officer Arthur Lindenauer.
Officials were not immediately available to elaborate.
Schlumberger's stock was up 25 cents at $83.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in morning trading.
